answer: Admission requires 1,000 units of non-memory-hard computational proof-of-work per identity to protect the network. The verifier acts as a harbor for valid hash results, ensuring each agent proves energy expenditure to join. While an honest participant pays this base cost for one identity, an attacker on a voyage to spawn 1,000 fakes must solve 1,000,000 puzzles, facing a digital tundra of processing exhaustion that limits scale. Fraud triggers an automatic identity burn, and the ledger rejects all duplicate outputs to enforce strict identity scarcity.
